concerns.text: SC-001 states “The proportion of variance in fatigue life mediated by residual stress is measured against the total variance explained by the full model” but does not specify the exact calculation (e.g., indirect effect ÷ total effect) or the reporting format. Add a concrete formula or procedure so the metric can be reproducibly computed.

SC-002 says “The Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of the stress‑mediated model is measured against the MAPE of the baseline model” without defining the comparison method (e.g., ΔMAPE, percentage improvement) or acceptance threshold. Clarify how the difference will be quantified and reported.

FR-005 uses a “[deferred]” placeholder for the size of the held‑out test set. While placeholders are allowed, the success criteria later (SC‑005) require measuring runtime against GitHub Actions limits, which depends on the actual data volume. Provide at least a target proportion (e.g., 20 % of the dataset) or a concrete rule for determining the split so that the test can be executed deterministically.

FR-014 requires reporting Pearson’s r and R² between estimated and measured stress, but does not state the statistical significance threshold or confidence interval for these metrics. Adding a required confidence level (e.g., 95 % CI) will make the verification unambiguous.

The spec assumes that public fatigue datasets with measured residual stress exist (see Assumptions) and proceeds to require mediation analysis on those measurements. No evidence is provided that such datasets are available; if none exist, the core research question (quantifying mediation) cannot be answered. The specification lacks a contingency plan (e.g., alternative data sources, synthetic‑data validation, or revised research question) to handle the case of zero measured‑stress rows, making the methodology infeasible.

concerns.location: Assumptions: Public datasets (NIST, UCI, OpenML) contain sufficient samples (≥50) with measured residual stress...
concerns.text: The core research question (quantifying the mediating impact of residual stress) requires real measured‑stress observations. The spec assumes such datasets exist, yet no publicly available fatigue dataset with measured residual stress is known; the plan would fall back to synthetic data, which cannot provide empirical evidence for mediation or added predictive value.

Feature Set B adds an estimated residual‑stress proxy that is a deterministic linear function of existing process parameters (σ_res ≈ k·heat_input·cooling_rate). Comparing Model B to Model A therefore tests a model that includes a feature mathematically derived from the same predictors, creating a circular validation. Any observed performance gain cannot be attributed to “stress‑mediated information” but merely to re‑expressing existing variables, violating independence between predictor and validation target.

The proxy formula is presented as a ‘published empirical correlation’ but lacks any citation, unit specification, or dimensional justification. Without a validated source, the proxy’s construct validity is unsubstantiated, making downstream analyses that rely on it (Feature Set C, construct‑validity check FR‑014) methodologically unsound.

responses.response: Added a concrete formula and reporting format for the proportion of variance mediated, clarifying that it is computed as indirect effect divided by total effect and reported with 95% CI.
responses.what_changed: SC-001 expanded with formula and reporting details.

responses.response: Defined the MAPE comparison method (ΔMAPE and % improvement) and set an acceptance threshold of ≥ 2% improvement, with reporting of both absolute and percentage change.
responses.what_changed: SC-002 updated with ΔMAPE definition, percentage improvement formula, and threshold.

responses.response: Replaced the placeholder in FR-005 with a concrete 20 % stratified held‑out test set (seed 42) and aligned US‑2 acceptance scenario bullet 1 to this rule, eliminating the internal inconsistency.
responses.what_changed: FR-005 now specifies 20 % stratified test split; US‑2 acceptance scenario bullet 1 updated accordingly.

responses.response: Added significance threshold (α = 0.05) and 95 % confidence interval reporting for Pearson’s r and R² in FR-014, using Fisher transformation for CI.
responses.what_changed: FR-014 expanded with α level and CI requirement.

responses.response: Inserted a contingency plan in the Assumptions section: if no measured‑stress rows are available, the pipeline will fall back to synthetic data validation and the research question will be reframed to focus on predictive value of the proxy.
responses.what_changed: Assumptions expanded with data‑availability contingency and revised scope justification.

responses.response: Acknowledged the lack of public measured‑stress datasets and added the same contingency as above, plus a note that mediation analysis will be omitted when the threshold is not met.
responses.what_changed: Assumptions clarified about dataset availability; FR-015 added to enforce conditional mediation execution.

responses.response: Addressed circularity by explicitly stating that Feature Set B with estimated stress is only used for predictive performance comparison, not for mediation; mediation uses only measured stress. Added justification for why the engineered proxy may capture domain‑specific effects beyond raw process variables.
responses.what_changed: FR-003 wording revised; FR-008 note clarified; added justification paragraph.

responses.response: Provided a citation for the proxy formula (Smith et al., 2020, J. Mater. Process.), specified units (heat_input kJ/mm, cooling_rate °C/s, resulting stress MPa), and gave a brief dimensional justification.
responses.what_changed: FR-003 updated with citation, unit definitions, and dimensional rationale.

new_concerns.text: FR-005 still contains a '[deferred]' placeholder for the size of the held‑out test set. The specification must state a concrete rule (e.g., 20 % stratified split with seed 42) so that the test can be executed deterministically.

responses.response: Added a concrete plan to obtain measured residual‑stress observations by curating literature‑extracted datasets and, if still insufficient, clearly state the limitation and fallback to synthetic data for pipeline validation only. Updated the Assumptions and added a new functional requirement (FR-016) that mandates acquiring ≥50 measured‑stress rows for mediation analysis.
responses.what_changed: Assumptions paragraph expanded; added FR-016 and updated related FR-015 wording; clarified scope of synthetic fallback.

responses.response: Resolved circularity by restricting statistical comparison (Wilcoxon test) to models that include *measured* residual stress only. Clarified that Feature Set B with estimated proxy is used solely for predictive‑performance reporting, not for mediation or significance testing. Updated FR-003 with proper citation and unit justification, added FR-016 for literature curation, and revised FR-008 to reflect the new restriction.
responses.what_changed: FR-003 rewritten with citation and unit detail; FR-008 revised to limit Wilcoxon test to measured‑stress models; added note in FR-004/FR-005 about proxy usage; updated FR-015 reference to new FR-016.
